business_rules.statement: Support sessions are read-only without exception, reason-required and ticket-linked, time-boxed with a two-hour default, tenant-visible for the whole session with an End-session control, and mirrored to the tenant's own audit trail.
A data repair is not support: anything that changes tenant data goes through the compliance-emergency path, which Support cannot open.
One tenant per session; no in-place extension; actions never exceed the declared scope.
business_rules.enforcement_point: server-side scope enforcement independent of the interface

business_rules.statement: Session scope is fixed at open and is not recomputed from role; no open session gains write capability.
Tenant termination of a support session is immediate and unconditional; a failed termination is recorded rather than hidden.
business_rules.enforcement_point: session machinery, time box as backstop

business_rules.statement: Session history is never deleted; no session survives disablement. Anonymisation applies to worker personal data and not to platform access records.
Exactly one Tenant Admin is seeded per tenant by the platform side; the account holds no platform authority; an unactivated account opens no session.
Only five roles exist; the last Tenant Admin cannot be removed; the last approver cannot be removed while a Job exists.
Only Tenant, Site, and Area scopes exist at V1; scope never crosses tenants; a failed refresh under-shows rather than over-shows.

A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry; configuration writes are blocked under soft suspension while run creation continues; no package-borne change is shown as in force before device acknowledgement.
No anonymisation occurs in Regulated-Industry mode; already-anonymised identities are never restored, since anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.
The creator can never approve the same Job; an approver role must exist whenever a Job exists.
The audit log is append-only and immutable on every path; an interrupted export produces no file; tamper-evidence is not claimed at V1.
Every Severity 1 runtime event creates a Critical anomaly automatically; resolution requires a closure note; the register is independent of notification delivery.
Permission is evaluated at write time, not at screen load; the last Tenant Admin cannot be removed.
No posture weaker than notify-only is accepted; clearance duration is uniform at tenant level; per-device posture is reported honestly.

Recertification stays open under soft suspension; no worker-facing message appears under soft or hard; the soft exit is an explicit operator signal and no tenant-state transition keys on a payment event.
The worker message matches the source string verbatim; no device is reported locked before it confirms; only the compliance-emergency path enters afterwards.

Every difference carries a classification and a treatment; late data inside the window folds in flagged and after finish follows audited recompute; skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All.
At least one Tenant Admin exists at every moment; worker departure reassigns before archiving; late captures from an archived worker are dual-flagged inside the window.
No self-registration exists; an unactivated account opens no session.
The Supervisor cannot resolve sync conflicts; the Supervisor cannot release a lot hold; multi-role is additive and audited by identity.
Qualification validation runs at assignment, run start, and override screens; no Client Command Center action can pause or stop a run; commands are reported per device.

Pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker; exactly two in-flight modifications are permitted (substitution and end-time extension); each worker who actually worked counts one Worker-Shift.
A Supervisor request never releases a hold; the note is mandatory; release is reported per device.
A categorised reason is mandatory; a never-held qualification requires the Quality Manager; a second clearance in the same Area in the same shift routes to the Quality Manager.
Supervisors view conflicts and never resolve them; skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All; work never waits on conflict review.
business_rules.enforcement_point: server-side refusal; panel is a review instrument

business_rules.statement: An escalation never resolves to nobody; fallback deliveries are visibly marked; the fallback default awaits DEC-NOSHIFT-001.
The worker completes the current run; there is no grace period beyond it; there is no on-device worker override.
A queued command survives its issuer's role change; no further grants are possible after removal.
business_rules.enforcement_point: command state independent of granter authority

business_rules.statement: Job Owner is reassignable and confers no permissions; worker departure reassigns before archiving; open step executions close as abandoned with the reason recorded.
A Quality Manager may cancel any run within scope; the Qualification Calendar horizon is 60 days.
Release is hers alone with no exceptions; no Client Command Center action reaches a specification or evaluation gate; review aging highlights fire at 24, 48, and 72 hours.
Every Severity 1 event creates a Critical anomaly automatically with its containment record; resolution requires a closure note; reclassification requires a recorded reason.
Only a Quality Manager identity can release; release is reported per device; no device resumes work on a held lot before applying the release.
No role performs two stages on one submission; the Release Authority cannot be bypassed; an incomplete locale blocks publication.
No proposal is auto-approved; undecided proposals never expire; the decision is made exactly once with no second approval.
Late arrivals inside the window fold in flagged and recompute; arrivals after the window are rejected; post-finish corrections preserve the prior output.
No gate item executes without a decision; no gate item silently expires; composed-agent approval never appears in this queue.
No role on any surface can override a specification or evaluation gate; the Client Command Center cannot pause or stop a run, edit any record, or create Jobs or runs.
business_rules.applies_to: the two hard gates and the four absolute exclusions

business_rules.statement: Never-held clearances require Quality Manager authorisation; repeat clearances in one Area on one shift route to her; clearance duration is uniform at tenant level.
An issued release survives its issuer's role change; a hold is never left without a possible releaser.
Skew-flagged conflicts are excluded from Resolve All; a conflict beyond specification limits becomes a deviation; post-finish corrections preserve the prior output and flag late data.
An approver exists at every moment while a Job exists; no workflow retains an unreachable Release Authority.
Every surface the auditor reaches is read-only; the Client Command Center is entirely unreachable.
Every Client Command Center decision is readable from the Delivery Operations Hub record; the log is append-only and immutable; the auditor's own export is audited.
Every rendering carries a data-as-of timestamp; reports are never presented as real-time; both namings of set 4 are preserved under DEC-REPORT-001.
Every published version carries Author, Reviewer, and Release Authority identities that are not the same person twice; prior versions remain permanently readable.
Acknowledge and resolve are distinct timestamped states; fallback deliveries are visibly marked; an escalation never resolves to nobody.
Every capture carries device time and server-receipt time; skew-flagged writes are identifiable; unsynced captures are named rather than absent.
Every gate outcome produces a decision record retained for the record's full term; raw reasoning is never exposed to a tenant.
The Quality Manager's audit access is scoped to Summary and run-state events; the auditor's equals the Tenant Admin's.
A scope change is a permission change and is audited; no self-service widening exists.
The audit log continues to be written under soft and hard suspension; compliance suspension blocks the auditor's login like everyone else's.
No self-registration exists; attribution follows the login, never the device; worker_type produces no operational difference at V1.
A Worker holds no scope-assignment authority; self-assignment is impossible at V1; no silent posture exists (notify-only is the floor).
A complete run executes with no connectivity at any point; no gate can be overridden on the device by any worker; sync is never a worker action; a worker cannot cancel or terminally complete a run.

Evidence is immutable at creation on every surface; media never reaches the device gallery; a quarantined capture is neither accepted nor discarded; the renderable capture-type set matches the authored set.
Pre-substitution steps stay attributed to the original worker; a worker cannot substitute or cancel; a pause by one worker never pauses the run for others.
A sync is forced before every sign-off; the worker's session is not ended by the step-up; a substitute sign-off is recorded in full and never a silent skip.
business_rules.enforcement_point: forced sync at designated high-risk action

business_rules.statement: Notice text equals the mandatory republish description; no notice interrupts an in-flight run; general inbox notifications carry no read obligation.

A complete run executes with no connectivity; severity classification occurs at capture, offline; a Severity 1 hold is placed locally and immediately; no surface implies the offline device received or applied anything.
Nothing is machine-translated at runtime; coaching absence never unblocks a gate; a single dismissal raises no supervisor signal.
Gates, specification checks, severity classification, and the Severity 1 hold all continue during any pause or outage; authored Work Instructions are always available as the guidance fallback.
business_rules.enforcement_point: deterministic backbone has no off switch

business_rules.statement: No on-device worker override exists; a blocked run parks rather than stalling the worker; no worker may write their own qualification.
Reassignment applies the same qualification rules as any assignment; reassignment is reported per device and never as instant.
The compliance-suspension message matches the source string verbatim; all local data is preserved; no worker-facing message appears under soft or hard suspension.
A final sync is attempted whenever the device is reachable; a pending wipe is never reported as complete; lost captures are named in a reconciliation statement.
Sync resumes automatically and is never a worker action; an interrupted drain resumes rather than restarting; the worker never sees conflict review.

Reassignment precedes archival; open step executions close as abandoned with the reason recorded; late captures from an archived worker are dual-flagged inside the window; anonymisation never occurs in Regulated-Industry mode.
No override exists on any surface for any role for a specification gate or the evaluation gate.
business_rules.applies_to: all nine roles, all five surfaces

business_rules.statement: Every out-of-bound value is rejected at entry with the bound stated.
No artificial intelligence participates in detection or classification.
business_rules.enforcement_point: device classification layer; no model on the trigger path

business_rules.statement: Every release is attributable to a Quality Manager identity; no agent holds any release capability.
No agent output reaches a worker or changes a record ungated, without a human gate or pre-authorised policy; the platform never invents content, rules, or thresholds.
Every audited action names a human identity or an approved policy that names one; the audit log records identity and action, never an acting-as-role fiction.
No operational content is readable without a named session; record-level operational content is reached only through one of the three named, audited, session-scoped access classes.
business_rules.applies_to: all four platform roles including the root

business_rules.statement: Creator and approver identities are never the same on any Job; where the creator also holds the approver role the platform routes to a second qualified approver.
Every published version carries three distinct signing identities.

The root-account count is exactly one at all times; every console account maps to a root creation event; there is no self-registration, no password-only path, and no role-escalation path except the root acting.
No surface reports a command as applied before device acknowledgement; commands apply at the device's next sync, in order.
No worker writes any qualification; qualifications are supervisor-entered with full audit and self-attestation is not permitted.
No evidence record can be mutated or deleted on any surface, including through the compliance-emergency path, which writes rather than erases.
business_rules.applies_to: all nine roles, all five surfaces

business_rules.statement: No purge path exists; shortening retention moves data rather than removing it; deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.
All six invariants refuse every account including the root, through the interface and directly.
business_rules.enforcement_point: server-side refusal independent of the interface
business_rules.applies_to: evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, one-transaction audit guarantee

business_rules.statement: No card's terminal safe state is "the action succeeds with a warning".
All eighty-one modules appear exactly once, with counts nineteen, eighteen derived, thirteen, twelve, and nineteen.
No claim of complete coverage is made anywhere in this chapter while any referenced decision remains open.
No storyboard shows a command as applied on a device that the same storyboard shows as offline at that moment.
Every storyboard crossing a recorded contradiction names its DEC-* identifier and preserves both readings.

Five rules bind every storyboard: no impermissible outcome; no contradiction resolved by picking a side; every storyboard reaches a terminal safe state; every material step names audit evidence; all five surfaces accounted for at every material step.
An action that cannot be audited does not happen, under the one-transaction audit guarantee.
Every panel that depicts a prohibited action renders it as a disabled action with a reason, never as an omitted control, unless the control does not exist at all — stated explicitly.
The catalog uses the capture, command, and notification vocabularies without collapsing any of them, and the word "synced" never appears as a standalone state.
A notification never enforces anything: enforcement is on-device deterministic logic, a command-channel action, or a server-side gate.
Server-receipt time is authoritative for ordering at sync; beyond the tenant's clock-skew threshold the device's timestamps stop being trusted to decide anything.

decisions.question: Should a tenant have a standing per-engineer support exclusion list?
options: reliance on the End-session control alone
decisions.impact: A tenant's objection currently depends on repeated manual termination.

decisions.question: Role-set definition question referenced on Tenant Admin role assignment.
decisions.impact: Governs the fixed five tenant roles and Studio role model.

decisions.question: What ordering, if any, do 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' denote across five additive, non-hierarchical roles?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — records that Supervisor+ and QM+ are undefined as an ordering
decisions.impact: Role sets must be reported literally rather than as a rank; 'higher authority' for substitute sign-off needs a decided definition.

decisions.question: What volume ceilings apply to audit-log exports?
decisions.impact: Large export ranges must be segmented; no partial file is delivered as if complete.

decisions.question: How does a tenant exit soft suspension — explicit operator signal or automatically on payment?
options: explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console
decisions.adopted_working_position: Exit is by the client's platform team as an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console
decisions.impact: No tenant-state transition keys on a payment event.

decisions.question: What is the fallback default when no on-shift holder exists for an escalation target role?
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — carried as an open drafting item
decisions.impact: Fallback delivery to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback.

decisions.impact: Governs Anomaly Register resolution semantics.

decisions.question: Lane B learned-change pipeline question.
decisions.impact: Governs auto-publish of approved learned changes.

decisions.question: Package field question affecting Lane B package-borne values.
decisions.impact: Governs which values ride the package versus server-only.

decisions.question: What is the identity of the five standard report data sets, given set 4 differs between §4.10.5 and §6.12.1?
decisions.status: open client item — both namings preserved
decisions.impact: The identity of all five standard report data sets is an open client item.

decisions.question: Should the platform carry a first-class audit finding object?
decisions.impact: Audit findings are the main output of the auditor role and currently have no home.

decisions.question: What is the activation lifetime for an issued worker credential?
decisions.impact: Governs credential issuance and activation windows.

decisions.question: Which set of seven capture types is the contract's? §1.7 and §7.8.3 name one set of seven; §5.5.3 names a different seven.
decisions.adopted_working_position: the contract names the adopted §5.5.3 seven while the difference stays recorded in the card
decisions.impact: Determines the renderable and authorable capture-type set.

decisions.question: How is the required final sync attempt reconciled for an offline device that never returns before a wipe?
decisions.impact: The source requires a final sync attempt an offline device cannot perform and sets no bound.

decisions.question: At reconnection, do captures upload before or after pending commands are pulled?
options: Option C — stop-class commands, then the full capture upload with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands
decisions.adopted_working_position: stop-class commands, then the full capture upload with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted on 2026-08-14 at Option C, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Both source readings preserved; governs reconnection exchange ordering.

decisions.question: How is agent gating declared?
options: Option C — gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted on 2026-08-14 at Option C, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Both source readings preserved in its card.

decisions.question: How is root custody recovered?
decisions.impact: A proposed standby root is refused; exactly one root at all times.

decisions.question: Which named compliance standards require deletion?
decisions.impact: Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it; the list is owed by the client.

decisions.question: Anonymisation policy question.
decisions.impact: Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.

decisions.question: Retrieval-from-archive question.
decisions.impact: Governs retrievability of tiered data.

decisions.question: What is the canonical Standards and Operations Studio module count?
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — no canonical Studio module count exists in the source; any count is derived
decisions.impact: The Studio branch of the 81-module inventory is derived, not canonical.

decisions.question: Is the per-run work package cryptographically signed and verified on the device before execution?
options: sign at generation and verify at staging
decisions.status: newly raised in this chapter — not in the canon's contradiction register
decisions.impact: An unverified package is an unverified deterministic safety layer.

decisions.question: At which instant is the package version pinned when assignment and staging happen at different times?
options: stage at shift start / lazy pull mid-shift (§7.6)
decisions.impact: Determines which limits were in force for a run — the audit receipt the version number exists to be.

decisions.question: Where does an unacknowledged shift-handoff brief escalate, given there is no Plant Manager role?
options: Plant Manager view after a 30-minute grace period (§6.13.3)
the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as fallback
decisions.status: newly raised in this chapter; related to DEC-ROLE-001 but distinct
decisions.impact: An escalation with no resolvable target silently resolves to nobody.

decisions.question: After a tenant terminates a support session from the banner, may the same engineer immediately open a new session on the same ticket?
decisions.status: newly raised in this chapter — not specified in the Statement of Work
decisions.impact: Without a rule, the tenant's End-session control is advisory rather than effective.

decisions.question: How long may a compliance-suspension device lock command remain pending for a device that never reconnects?
options: bound the command's validity and expire it explicitly
decisions.status: newly raised in this chapter; analogous to DEC-WIPE-001 but concerns lock, not erasure
decisions.impact: A tenant under compliance suspension with an offline device has an unbounded window in which work continues.

decisions.question: Does the Tenant Admin role hold Client Command Center access?
options: §6.1.3 omits the Tenant Admin from the surface's user groups
§4.8.1 gives broad tenant configuration remit with no stated exclusion
grant read access without any of the ten operational actions
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — newly raised in this chapter
decisions.impact: Determines whether the closed set of ten actions has a fourth eligible role.

contradictions.description: Soft-suspension exit: the source carries an operator-signal reading and an automatic-on-payment reading; the card adopts the operator-signal position without resolving the source.
conflicting_values: explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console
automatic on payment

contradictions.description: 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' are used by the authority matrices without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
conflicting_values: Supervisor+ / QM+ implies a rank
five roles are additive and non-hierarchical with no ordering

contradictions.description: The identity of standard report data set 4 differs between §4.10.5 and §6.12.1; the identity of all five sets is an open client item.
conflicting_values: §4.10.5 naming of set 4
§6.12.1 naming of set 4

contradictions.description: Capture-type set: §1.7 and §7.8.3 name one set of seven while §5.5.3 names a different seven; the contract adopts the §5.5.3 seven and records the difference.
conflicting_values: §1.7 / §7.8.3 seven capture types
§5.5.3 seven capture types

contradictions.description: Reconnection ordering: the source does not fix whether captures upload before or after pending commands are pulled; both readings are preserved and Option C is adopted.
conflicting_values: captures upload first
pending commands pulled first
Option C: stop-class commands, then full capture upload, then enabling-class commands

contradictions.description: Releaser invariant: the source states the approver invariant explicitly and does not state a releaser invariant; the card applies the same logic and flags it as an Assumption rather than assuming silently.
conflicting_values: approver invariant stated in source
releaser invariant inferred by analogy

contradictions.description: Wipe: the source requires a final sync attempt that an offline device cannot perform and sets no bound for a device that never returns.
conflicting_values: final sync attempt required before erasure
offline device cannot perform a final sync

contradictions.description: No canonical Standards and Operations Studio module count exists in the source; the eighteen-module inventory is derived.
conflicting_values: eighteen derived Studio modules
no canonical count in source

contradictions.description: Tenant Admin access to the Client Command Center: §6.1.3 names supervisors, quality managers and plant-manager-scoped supervisors and omits the Tenant Admin, while §4.8.1 gives broad remit without stating an exclusion; only the Read-only Auditor's exclusion is stated outright.
conflicting_values: §6.1.3 omits the Tenant Admin from the surface's user groups
§4.8.1 grants configuration and user-management remit with no Command Center exclusion

contradictions.description: Shift-handoff escalation: §6.13.3 flags an unacknowledged brief on the Plant Manager view after a 30-minute grace period, while §3.5 fixes five roles and Plant Manager is a persona, not a role.
conflicting_values: escalate to the Plant Manager view after 30 minutes (§6.13.3)
five fixed roles; Plant Manager is a persona not a role (§3.5)

contradictions.description: Package pinning instant: §4.6.1 pins the package at assignment while §7.6 stages known runs at shift start and pulls mid-shift assignments lazily, leaving the staged version ambiguous when a version publishes in between.
conflicting_values: pin at assignment (§4.6.1)
stage at shift start / lazy pull mid-shift (§7.6)

contradictions.description: Package integrity verification is not specified: §7.10.1 states delivery and pinning and §7.11 states an app-managed encrypted store, but neither states package integrity verification.
conflicting_values: package signed and verified before execution
no verification specified

contradictions.description: Support re-open after tenant termination is unspecified: §4.12.2 and §8.15 give the End-session control but neither states a cool-down, a re-open limit, or notification of a re-open.
conflicting_values: End-session control is effective
no re-open rule makes it advisory

contradictions.description: Compliance-suspension device lock has no bounded pending period: §4.2.3 locks devices at next contact but the source does not bound the pending period or state the outcome if contact never occurs.
conflicting_values: lock at next contact
unbounded pending window for a device that never reconnects

contradictions.description: A standing per-engineer tenant exclusion list is not specified in the Statement of Work; the tenant's objection currently depends on repeated manual termination.
conflicting_values: End-session control alone is the operative mechanism
a standing exclusion list is expected by tenants

contradictions.description: No finding object exists in the platform, yet audit findings are the main output of the Read-only Auditor role.
conflicting_values: no finding object exists (not specified in the SoW)
auditor role's main output is findings

controls.label: action 10 (grant a qualification clearance)
controls.effect: Grants a clearance applied at the device's next sync.

controls.label: action 8 (reassignment)
controls.effect: Executes reassignment through the owning Delivery Operations Hub service.

controls.label: action 4 (release a lot hold)
controls.effect: Releases a lot hold; the only role with release capability.

controls.effect: Creates a release request item; the note is mandatory.

controls.label: Acknowledge and annotate the shift handoff brief

controls.effect: Re-runs the rule-based evaluation once agents return.

controls.label: Mark relevant / not relevant (prior case relevance)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A write path is reachable inside a support session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Suspend all support sessions platform-wide
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No support session open anywhere; tenant data untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A closed defect; compare support-session actions against write events, expected count zero

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant termination signal does not reach the console
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The time box expires
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Access ends by the box at the latest and the failed termination is recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Confirmed closure; compare termination requests to closures

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Console and tenant session records disagree
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Treat the tenant's record as authoritative for the tenant's own question
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No access event is invisible to the tenant
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Records agree; compare console session records to tenant-mirrored events

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A package-borne setting fails to distribute
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Name the devices still on the prior bundle
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prior bundle stays in force on the floor and the platform says so
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Distribution completes; report adoption lag

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scoped index does not refresh
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Show an explicit scope-updating state
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prior, narrower scope remains in force — under-visibility is the safe direction
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Index refresh

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Notification delivery fails on both channels for a Critical anomaly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The register carries the anomaly independently of any notification
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The anomaly is visible and open; a notification is never the only mechanism
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolution with a closure note

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Suspension state does not reach a device
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Cache-validity expiry stops the device independently
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Devices stop accepting new work when their cached trust expires; captured work is preserved and syncs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: State lift; compare intended state against per-device applied state

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device never contacts the platform under compliance suspension
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-queue the stop at every contact
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Trust-window expiry blocks authentication independently
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No new work anywhere; local data preserved on every device; the outstanding devices named with their ages
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reviewed exit; drain queues, disposition stopped runs, recompute Summaries under the audited-recompute rule, produce a named restoration statement

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device does not acknowledge a supervisor command
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reassign the run to a worker on a responsive device
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run parks or waits; nothing is claimed as applied
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Command delivery; compare commands issued to commands acknowledged per device

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A release request does not reach the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The nobody-on-shift fallback delivers to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot stays held; production moves elsewhere or waits
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager decision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No Quality Manager exists at all for an escalation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The mandatory-role rules prevent a tenant with a Job from having no approver
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate to the Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot stays held or the run parks; safety is never traded for availability
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Acknowledgement; DEC-NOSHIFT-001 remains open

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A resolution path exists for a Supervisor on a sync conflict
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Freeze the resolution function
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Automatic resolution stands and work never waits on conflict review
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Quality Manager resolution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Package generation fails after release
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Mark the version published-not-distributable and block adoption
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prior version remains in force on every device and the platform says so
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Package generation; compare published versions to generated packages and device inventories

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Lane B auto-publish pipeline fails after approval
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Record the change as approved-not-published and notify the decider
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The originally configured value remains in force everywhere until a version is confirmed on each device
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Publication and distribution; list approved-not-in-force values with ages

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An override path exists for a specification or evaluation gate
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Freeze the affected surface
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The gate holds; the worker cannot advance without valid proof; the deviation is recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The deviation is handled properly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Upload is interrupted mid-capture
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The durable queue resumes where it left off
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A capture failing validation is quarantined with a recorded reason rather than accepted or discarded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The capture remains committed locally, counted honestly, and never presented as recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Upload completion; list captures committed locally but never accepted

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The offline period exceeds the credential-trust window
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: She continues on another device where one is available and connected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work stops with all local data preserved and a forced sync required; trust is never extended silently
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No suitable coaching asset exists
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The curated coaching default is used
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The authored Work Instructions carry the step
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A gate never opens because guidance was missing; guidance and gating are entirely separate
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Card availability

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The device wipe queue drains only partially before connectivity drops
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Halt the wipe and escalate with the exact list of undrained captures
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Device de-authorised, wipe pending, and the unsynced captures declared lost in a named reconciliation statement rather than quietly absent
failures_fallbacks.recovery: De-authorisation and credential reissue; mark affected runs incomplete and apply the audited-recompute rule

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The connection drops mid queue-drain
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The durable, resumable queue resumes where it left off
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Partial drain with the remainder retained and counted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing is discarded to make the queue look empty; media is evicted only after confirmed receipt plus an integrity check
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Full drain; compare device ledger to accepted ledger and produce the named statement

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An out-of-bound (looser-than-floor) value persists
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Enforce the stricter of the two values
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform never accepts an out-of-bound configuration
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A valid value; compare every tenant value against the register, expected violations zero

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A model call appears on the deviation trigger path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Disable the capability
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Detection and classification remain rule-based; the deterministic backbone has no off switch
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Deterministic integrity; assert no model call on the trigger path

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An agent output reaches a worker ungated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Emergency pause
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing reaches the floor without a human signature or an approved policy
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Human decision; assert every agent-originated change carries a human approval or a pre-authorised policy reference

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Two root accounts exist
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Disable the newer account
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Exactly one root, surplus disabled, incident escalated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restored uniqueness; continuous root-count assertion

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An invariant renders editable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Server-side refusal independent of the interface
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Freeze all settings writes
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Settings read-only and invariants intact
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Assert each invariant's stored state matches its enforced value

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A prohibition is documented but not enforced in code
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The prohibition is enforced server-side regardless of what any interface offers
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The affected function is frozen
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prior, safer behaviour stands and the gap is raised as a defect of the highest class
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A closed defect; reconciliation compares the prohibition list against enforcement test results

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A storyboard describes behaviour the rest of the blueprint no longer states (catalog divergence)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The cross-check step re-run whenever a referenced section changes
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Split the storyboard into branch A and branch B and carry both where the governing chapter is an unresolved DEC-*
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A storyboard marked blocked on decision, with the decision identifier named
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The client's decision landing; re-run of the cross-check across every storyboard referencing that decision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A storyboard identifier is reused or an audit block overlaps another's
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The lint in TEST-30-002 which resolves every identifier
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalation to the blueprint owner where a collision cannot be retired
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The colliding storyboard marked withheld in the register, present but not authoritative
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A single owning chapter being named; re-run of the identifier lint
